blocks.text: You can edit, delete, enable, or disable the alert rule that you've added.

blocks.item: From the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > Alert Notifications.
In the table, locate the alert rule you want to edit, click the Actions icon (), and select Edit.
See image.
The Edit Alert Rule page appears.
On the Edit Alert Rule page, in the General Information section, change the Alert Rule Name or Alert Rule Description as required, then click Next.
In the Notification Scope section, update the filters as required, then click Next.
In the Notifications section, update the notification channels as required, then click Next.
Review the changes and click Finish.
See image.
A message appears indicating that the alert rule is updated successfully.
Go to Data Security > DSPM > Alert Notifications.
In the table, locate the alert rule you want to edit, click the Actions icon (), and select Delete.
See image.
A confirmation message appears. Read the message and click Delete.
See image.

blocks.heading: Enabling or Disabling an Alert Rule

blocks.text: When you disable an alert rule, DSPM stops sending alert notifications to the configured third-party tools.
An alert rule is disabled with an exclamation mark on the alert name in the following scenarios:

blocks.item: The third-party tools are not configured while adding the alert rule.
The selected filters in the filter scope are deleted (e.g., policies are deleted, accounts are offboarded, or the business unit is deleted).

blocks.text: You can enable the alert rule only after at least one filter scope is available and at least one third-party tool is configured.
To enable or disable the alert rule:

blocks.item: Go to Data Security > DSPM > Alert Notifications.
Click the toggle under the State column to enable or disable the alert rule.
See image.
A confirmation message appears indicating that the alert rule is going to be enabled or disabled. Click Enable or Disable depending on the action.
See image.
